examples.ko: 이 협약에는 백 개가 넘는 가맹국이 서명했어요.
examples.en: More than a hundred member countries signed this agreement.

examples.ko: 유엔 가맹국은 모두 회의에 참석할 수 있어요.
examples.en: All UN member countries can attend the meeting.

examples.ko: 우리나라는 그 기구의 가맹국이 된 지 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been ten years since our country became a member of that organization.

examples.ko: 가맹국끼리 무역 문제를 놓고 회의를 열었어요.
examples.en: The member countries held a meeting about trade issues.
They decide by vote whether to accept a new member country.

examples.ko: 가맹국에는 회비를 내야 할 의무가 있어요.
examples.en: Member countries have a duty to pay membership fees.

explain: 국제기구나 조약에 가입한 나라를 말하고, 뉴스나 수업에서 주로 나와요. 같은 뜻으로 '회원국'이 더 쉽고 자주 들려요. 프랜차이즈의 '가맹점'과 같은 '가맹'이 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to countries that have joined an international organization or treaty, and it mostly appears in news and lessons. '회원국' has the same meaning and is easier and more common to hear. It shares '가맹' with '가맹점', a franchise store.

examples.ko: 새 정부의 각료 명단이 오늘 발표됐어요.
examples.en: The new government's list of cabinet members was announced today.
The cabinet members discussed next year's budget at the meeting.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 예전에 각료로 일한 경험이 있어요.
examples.en: That politician has experience working as a cabinet member.

examples.ko: 총리가 각료들에게 현장을 직접 살펴보라고 했어요.
examples.en: The prime minister told the cabinet members to check the site in person.
They say he was offered a cabinet post but turned it down.

examples.ko: 각료 세 명이 대통령과 함께 해외 순방길에 올랐어요.
examples.en: Three cabinet members set off on an overseas trip with the president.

explain: 한 사람을 부를 때는 '장관'이라고 하고, 각료는 '각료 회의', '각료 인선'처럼 장관들을 묶어서 말할 때 많이 써요. 뉴스와 정치 기사에서 자주 나오고 일상 대화에서는 드물어요.
explain_en: For one person you say '장관' (minister); 각료 is used when talking about ministers as a group, as in '각료 회의' or '각료 인선'. It appears often in news and political articles but rarely in everyday talk.

examples.ko: 개도국에 학교를 짓는 봉사 활동에 참여했어요.
examples.en: I took part in a volunteer project building schools in developing countries.
Korea, too, used to be called a developing country.
The gap between developed and developing countries is still large.

examples.ko: 이번 회의에서 개도국 지원 문제를 다뤘어요.
examples.en: This meeting dealt with the issue of aid to developing countries.

examples.ko: 개도국 학생들을 위한 장학금이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new scholarship for students from developing countries was created.

examples.ko: 개도국은 기후 변화의 피해를 더 크게 입어요.
examples.en: Developing countries suffer greater damage from climate change.

explain: '개발도상국'의 줄임말이에요. 뉴스와 기사에서는 자주 보지만 말로 할 때는 '개발도상국'이라고 하는 경우도 많아요. 짝이 되는 말은 '선진국'이에요.
explain_en: This is the shortened form of '개발도상국'. You often see it in news and articles, but in speech people often say the full '개발도상국'. Its counterpart is '선진국' (developed country).

examples.ko: 거국적 차원에서 이 문제를 풀어야 해요.
examples.en: We have to solve this problem at the level of the whole nation.

examples.ko: 나라 전체가 참여하는 거국적인 행사가 열려요.
examples.en: A nationwide event with the whole country taking part will be held.

examples.ko: 정부가 거국적으로 재난 극복 운동을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The government started a nationwide campaign to overcome the disaster.
During the World Cup, the whole nation was in a cheering mood.

examples.ko: 거국적 노력 없이는 쉽게 해결되지 않아요.
examples.en: It won't be easily solved without an effort by the whole nation.

examples.ko: 이번 사업은 거국적 지원이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: This project definitely needs support from the entire nation.

explain: 뒤에 '차원', '운동', '응원', '지원' 같은 명사가 와서 나라 전체가 한마음으로 한다는 느낌을 줘요. '거국적인', '거국적으로'로도 자주 써요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스나 연설에서 더 많이 들려요.
explain_en: It is followed by nouns like '차원', '운동', '응원' and '지원', giving the sense that the whole country acts as one. It is also commonly used as '거국적인' and '거국적으로'. You hear it more in news and speeches than in everyday talk.

examples.ko: 공복에 약을 먹으면 속이 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: Taking medicine on an empty stomach can hurt your stomach.
I have a health checkup tomorrow, so I must go without eating.

examples.ko: 공복 혈당을 재려면 아침 식사 전에 해야 해요.
examples.en: To measure fasting blood sugar, you have to do it before breakfast.

examples.ko: 공복 상태로 열두 시간 있어야 해요.
examples.en: You have to stay fasting for twelve hours.

examples.ko: 공복일 때 마트에 가면 이것저것 많이 사요.
examples.en: When I go to the mart hungry, I buy a lot of things.
If I stay hungry for long, I get a headache.

explain: 밥을 먹지 않아 배가 빈 상태를 말해요. 병원이나 약 설명서에서 '공복에', '공복 혈당'처럼 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '빈속'이 더 편하게 쓰이고, 반대로 밥 먹은 뒤는 '식후'라고 해요. 소리가 같은 '공복(公僕)'은 '공무원'을 뜻하는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It means the stomach is empty because you have not eaten. You see '공복에' and '공복 혈당' in hospitals and on medicine labels. In casual speech 빈속 is more common, and the opposite is 식후 (after a meal). The homophone 공복(公僕) is a different word meaning 'public servant'.

examples.en: People and animals coexist in the city.
Several cultures coexisted in one country.
It is a street where tradition and modernity coexist.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 의견이 공존할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Different opinions can coexist.
To coexist with neighbors, you have to consider each other.
It was a day when sadness and joy coexisted.

explain: 'A와 B가 공존하다'처럼 서로 다른 것이 한곳에 함께 있을 때 써요. '같이 살다'는 사람과 동물의 생활에 쓰지만 공존하다는 생각이나 문화 같은 개념에도 써요. '공생하다'는 서로 도움을 주고받는 관계라서 달라요.
explain_en: Use it as 'A와 B가 공존하다' when different things exist in the same place. 같이 살다 is for the living of people or animals, but 공존하다 also covers ideas and cultures. 공생하다 (symbiosis) is different: it means helping each other.

en: give relief to; rescue and aid

examples.en: The firefighters gave aid to the injured people.

examples.ko: 재난 지역의 주민들을 구호하는 단체에 기부했어요.
examples.en: I donated to an organization that gives relief to residents of disaster areas.

examples.ko: 먼저 부상자를 구호하고 나서 병원으로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: They first gave aid to the wounded and then moved them to the hospital.
There are not enough supplies to provide relief to the flood victims.

examples.ko: 적십자는 전쟁 난민을 구호하려고 현장에 갔어요.
examples.en: The Red Cross went to the site to help war refugees.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에서 다친 아이를 구호해 준 분이 있어요.
examples.en: Someone helped the injured child at the scene of the accident.

explain: '돕다'보다 훨씬 무겁고, 재난, 전쟁, 사고처럼 위험한 상황에서 사람을 구하고 돌볼 때만 써요. '구호 물품', '구호 단체'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요. 슬로건 뜻의 '구호'는 한자가 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is far heavier than '돕다' and is only used for rescuing and caring for people in dangerous situations such as disasters, wars, and accidents. It also appears as a noun in '구호 물품' (relief supplies) and '구호 단체' (relief organization). The '구호' meaning slogan is a different word with different Chinese characters.

examples.en: There is a military base near my house.
My older brother serves at a military unit in Gangwon Province.

examples.ko: 군부대 앞에서는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos in front of a military base.
The singers visited a military unit and performed.
During the flood, the military unit helped the village.

examples.ko: 군부대 근처에는 면회 온 가족을 위한 식당이 많아요.
examples.en: Near the base there are many restaurants for families who come to visit.

explain: 군인들이 모여 생활하고 훈련하는 단위나 그 장소를 말해요. '부대'라고 줄여서 말하기도 해요. 한국은 군 복무 문화가 있어서 '부대에 들어가다', '부대 면회'처럼 자주 들려요.
explain_en: 군부대 is the military unit or the place where soldiers live and train. It is often shortened to 부대. Because of military service in Korea, you hear phrases like 부대에 들어가다 and 부대 면회.

examples.en: We have to overcome the crisis both at home and abroad.
Internal and external conditions are not good.
The plan was postponed because of internal and external factors.
Assessments at home and abroad are divided.
Building trust both inside and outside is important.
It is a difficult time both domestically and internationally.

explain: '대내외적 위기'처럼 명사 앞에 쓰고, '대내외적으로' 형태의 부사로도 많이 써요. 나라뿐 아니라 회사나 단체의 안팎에도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '안팎으로'가 더 자연스럽고, '대내외적'은 뉴스나 발표에서 자주 들리는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '대내외적 위기', and is also common as the adverb '대내외적으로'. It applies to the inside and outside of a company or group as well as a country. In daily talk '안팎으로' sounds more natural, while '대내외적' is a stiff expression often heard in news and presentations.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 전체 표의 절반 가까이를 득표했어요.
examples.en: That candidate won close to half of all the votes.

examples.ko: 반장 선거에서 가장 많이 득표한 친구가 반장이 됐어요.
examples.en: The friend who got the most votes in the class president election became president.

examples.ko: 이번 선거에서 몇 퍼센트를 득표할지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder what percent of the vote they'll win in this election.

examples.ko: 후보들이 득표하려고 시장을 돌며 인사를 해요.
examples.en: Candidates go around the market greeting people to win votes.

examples.ko: 많이 득표했다고 해서 꼭 당선되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Getting many votes doesn't necessarily mean being elected.
He got fewer votes than first place and sadly lost.

explain: '표를 얻다'와 같은 내용인데, 선거 뉴스에서 짧게 말할 때 써요. '몇 표를/몇 퍼센트를 득표하다'처럼 얻은 표의 양이 같이 나오는 일이 많고, '득표율', '득표수'라는 말도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It means the same as '표를 얻다' (to get votes) but is used as a short form in election news. It often comes with the amount of votes, as in '몇 표를/몇 퍼센트를 득표하다'. It also helps to learn '득표율' (vote share) and '득표수' (vote count).

examples.ko: 그 의원은 정당 없이 무소속으로 출마했어요.
examples.en: That lawmaker ran as an independent, without a party.
An independent candidate won the election.

examples.ko: 저는 어느 동아리에도 속하지 않은 무소속이에요.
examples.en: I'm unaffiliated, not belonging to any club.

examples.ko: 무소속의 입장에서 두 당의 의견을 들었어요.
examples.en: From an independent's standpoint, I listened to both parties' views.

examples.ko: 그는 팀을 떠나 한동안 무소속 신세였어요.
examples.en: He left the team and was without a team for a while.
Since I'm independent, I don't take anyone's side.

explain: 선거와 정치 뉴스에서 '무소속 후보', '무소속 의원'처럼 가장 많이 나와요. 스포츠에서 소속 팀이 없는 선수에게도 쓰고, 반대는 '소속'이에요.
explain_en: It shows up most in election and political news, as in '무소속 후보' and '무소속 의원'. It's also used in sports for a player with no team, and the opposite is '소속'.

examples.en: The government started a nationwide campaign to save energy.

examples.ko: 이번 일은 범국민적 관심을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: This matter is drawing nationwide attention.
Many people took part in the nationwide campaign.
Protecting the environment takes an effort by the whole nation.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 노래는 범국민적 사랑을 받았어요.
examples.en: That singer's song was loved by the whole nation.
A consensus among the whole nation has to be reached first.

explain: 뉴스나 연설에서 '범국민적 운동/노력/관심'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '온 국민이', '전 국민이'라고 말하는 편이에요. '범세계적', '범시민적'처럼 '범-'이 붙으면 '전체가 함께'라는 느낌이 돼요.
explain_en: It is placed before a noun in news and speeches, as in '범국민적 운동/노력/관심'. In everyday talk people say '온 국민이' or '전 국민이' instead. With '범-', as in '범세계적', it carries the sense of everyone taking part together.

examples.en: Climate change is a worldwide problem.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 범세계적 인기를 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: That singer is gaining worldwide popularity.
It's hard to solve without global cooperation.
This brand is known all over the world.
Infectious diseases require a global response.

examples.ko: 범세계적 규모의 행사라서 준비할 것이 많아요.
examples.en: It's a global-scale event, so there is a lot to prepare.

explain: '세계적인'이 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이고, '범세계적'은 온 세상이 함께 관련된다는 무게가 있어서 뉴스나 글에서 많이 보여요. 주로 '문제, 협력, 대응' 같은 말 앞에 와요.
explain_en: '세계적인' is the easier everyday word, while '범세계적' carries the weight of the whole world being involved and shows up in news and writing. It mostly comes before words like '문제', '협력' and '대응'.

examples.ko: 제주도에서 본토까지 비행기로 한 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes an hour by plane from Jeju Island to the mainland.

examples.ko: 본토 사람들은 섬 문화를 잘 몰라요.
examples.en: People on the mainland don't know much about island culture.

examples.ko: 이 음식은 본토에서 먹는 맛과 달라요.
examples.en: This food tastes different from what you get in its home country.
I want to learn the native pronunciation.
I heard the typhoon will reach the mainland soon.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 본토 팬들에게 큰 사랑을 받아요.
examples.en: That singer is greatly loved by fans in the home country.

explain: '본토'는 섬이나 해외 영토에서 볼 때 중심이 되는 큰 땅이에요. 또 어떤 문화나 음식이 처음 생긴 곳을 말할 때도 써서 '본토 발음', '본토 맛'처럼 '원조'라는 느낌을 줘요.
explain_en: 본토 is the main body of land as seen from an island or overseas territory. It also means the place where something originated, so '본토 발음' or '본토 맛' gives the feel of the real original.

examples.ko: 관광객이 여러 곳으로 분산되어 덜 붐볐어요.
examples.en: The tourists spread out to several places, so it was less crowded.
We divided up the work, so the burden was spread out.

examples.ko: 주의가 분산되면 공부가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: When your attention is scattered, studying doesn't go well.

examples.ko: 투자가 한곳에 몰리지 않고 분산되는 게 안전해요.
examples.en: It's safer when investments are spread out rather than concentrated in one place.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 모여 있던 사람들이 분산됐어요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the crowd that had gathered dispersed.
Connections are being distributed across several servers.

explain: '주의가 분산되다', '위험이 분산되다', '인구가 분산되다'처럼 추상적인 것에 자주 써요. 반대말은 '집중되다'예요. 사람이 일부러 나누면 '분산하다', 저절로 흩어지면 '분산되다'예요. '흩어지다'는 훨씬 가볍고 일상적인 말이에요.
explain_en: It is often used with abstract things: 주의가 분산되다 (attention is scattered), 위험이 분산되다 (risk is spread), 인구가 분산되다 (the population is dispersed). Its opposite is 집중되다. When someone does it on purpose it is 분산하다; when it happens by itself it is 분산되다. 흩어지다 is a lighter, everyday word.

examples.ko: 회사는 투명한 공개로 고객의 의혹을 불식하려고 했어요.
examples.en: The company tried to wipe out customers' suspicions through transparent disclosure.

examples.ko: 이번 발표가 그런 불안을 불식했으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope this announcement puts that anxiety to rest.
The boss stepped in personally and put an end to the rumor.

examples.ko: 이 문제를 불식하지 못하면 팀 분위기가 계속 나빠질 거예요.
examples.en: If we can't clear up this problem, the team atmosphere will keep getting worse.

examples.ko: 정부는 국민의 오해를 불식하기 위해 설명회를 열었어요.
examples.en: The government held a briefing to dispel the public's misunderstanding.

examples.ko: 솔직하게 사과해야 불신을 불식할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only if you apologize honestly can you wipe out the distrust.

explain: 의혹, 불안, 오해, 편견, 불신처럼 좋지 않은 생각이나 분위기와 함께 써요. '없애다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스나 발표문에 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '없애다', '풀다'를 써요. '불식시키다'로도 쓰는데 뜻은 같아요.
explain_en: It goes with unwelcome ideas or moods such as suspicion, anxiety, misunderstanding, prejudice and distrust. It is stiffer than '없애다', so it appears in news and announcements, while daily talk uses '없애다' or '풀다'. '불식시키다' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The UN Secretary-General announced a new plan.
The secretary-general explained this year's budget at the meeting.

examples.ko: 우리 협회의 새 사무총장은 십 년 동안 일한 사람이에요.
examples.en: The new secretary-general of our association has worked here for ten years.
I sent a letter directly to the secretary-general.
I read the secretary-general's interview in the newspaper.
The atmosphere of the organization changed along with the new secretary-general.

explain: 큰 국제기구나 협회에서 일을 총괄하는 가장 높은 직위예요. '유엔 사무총장'처럼 기관 이름 뒤에 붙는 경우가 많아요. 작은 회사에서는 거의 쓰지 않고 '대표', '사장'을 써요.
explain_en: It is the top administrative post in a large international body or association. It usually follows the organization's name, as in '유엔 사무총장'. Small companies don't use it; they say '대표' or '사장'.

examples.ko: 산유국들은 석유 값이 오르면 수입이 늘어요.
examples.en: Oil-producing countries earn more when oil prices rise.
There are many large oil-producing countries in the Middle East.
Oil prices change depending on the decisions of oil-producing countries.

examples.ko: 우리나라는 산유국에서 석유를 많이 사 와요.
examples.en: Korea buys a lot of oil from oil-producing countries.
I traveled to a country known as an oil producer.
The positions of oil producers and consuming countries differ.

explain: 석유를 생산하는 나라를 말해요. 경제 뉴스에서 기름값이나 국제 정세를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요. 짝이 되는 말로 석유를 사 오는 나라를 가리키는 '소비국', '수입국'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to a country that produces oil. It often appears in economic news about fuel prices and international affairs. Counterparts include '소비국' and '수입국', countries that consume or import oil.

examples.en: Online shopping is very widespread these days.

examples.ko: 그 지역에서는 예전부터 불법 복제가 성행했어요.
examples.en: Illegal copying has been rampant in that area for a long time.
Fake goods are rampant, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 놀이는 조선 시대에 크게 성행했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this game was very popular in the Joseon period.

examples.ko: 배달 음식이 성행하는 동네에는 가게가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many shops in neighborhoods where food delivery thrives.

examples.ko: 한때 성행했던 만화방이 지금은 거의 없어요.
examples.en: The comic book cafes that once thrived are almost gone now.

explain: '유행하다'는 옷이나 노래처럼 잠깐 인기를 끄는 것에도 쓰지만, '성행하다'는 어떤 일이나 풍습이 활발히 이루어질 때 써요. 좋은 일뿐 아니라 불법, 가짜 같은 나쁜 현상에도 자주 써서 뉴스에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: '유행하다' can describe something with passing popularity like clothes or songs, whereas '성행하다' is used when a practice or activity is actively widespread. It is used for good things and also often for bad ones such as illegal acts or fakes, so you see it a lot in the news.

examples.en: The soldier walks with a rifle slung over the shoulder.

examples.ko: 영화 속 병사들이 소총으로 사격 연습을 해요.
examples.en: The soldiers in the movie practice shooting with rifles.
An old rifle is on display at the museum.

examples.ko: 소총은 권총보다 길고 멀리 쏠 수 있어요.
examples.en: A rifle is longer than a pistol and can shoot farther.
I learned how to clean a rifle at the training camp.

examples.ko: 경찰이 소총을 든 사람이 있다는 신고를 받았어요.
examples.en: The police received a report that someone was holding a rifle.

explain: 총 중에서 어깨에 대고 쏘는 긴 총을 가리켜요. 손에 쥐는 짧은 총은 '권총'이라고 해요. 군대, 뉴스, 영화에서 주로 듣는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to the long gun fired from the shoulder. The short gun held in one hand is a 권총. You mostly hear it in the military, news and films.

examples.en: The police sent the case to the prosecution yesterday.

examples.ko: 수사를 마치면 곧 서류를 송치할 거예요.
examples.en: Once the investigation is over, they will forward the documents soon.
I heard the department in charge decided to forward the case.
The police have not forwarded the case yet.

examples.ko: 사건을 먼저 송치해야 다음 단계로 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: The case has to be forwarded first before moving to the next step.

examples.ko: 어제 송치한 사건은 아직 검토 중이에요.
examples.en: The case forwarded yesterday is still under review.

explain: 주어는 보통 경찰이고, '사건을 검찰에/검찰로 송치하다'처럼 써요. 뉴스에서는 '검찰에 송치됐다'처럼 피동으로도 자주 나오지만, 말할 때는 이렇게 능동형으로 익혀 두면 충분해요.
explain_en: The subject is usually the police, as in '사건을 검찰에/검찰로 송치하다'. The news also uses the passive form like '검찰에 송치됐다', but learning this active form is enough for speaking.

examples.en: The police put handcuffs on the criminal.
A man in handcuffs went into the court.
In the movie, the hero slipped out of the handcuffs and escaped.
The handcuffs were too tight on the wrist.
A suspect in handcuffs appeared on the news.

examples.ko: 그는 수갑 때문에 손목에 자국이 생겼어요.
examples.en: He got marks on his wrists from the handcuffs.

explain: 수갑은 '채우다', '차다', '풀다'와 함께 써요. 누가 채우면 '수갑을 채우다', 내가 차면 '수갑을 차다'라고 해서 동사가 달라져요.
explain_en: 수갑 goes with 채우다, 차다, and 풀다. When someone puts them on another person it is '수갑을 채우다', and for the wearer it is '수갑을 차다', so the verb changes.

examples.en: The president tours three countries.
The minister returned after touring Asian countries.

examples.ko: 총리는 다음 달에 중동을 순방할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The prime minister plans to tour the Middle East next month.
During the tour they also met local business people.

examples.ko: 지역 곳곳을 순방해서 주민 의견을 들었어요.
examples.en: They toured all over the region and listened to residents' opinions.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 전국을 순방하며 선거운동을 했어요.
examples.en: That lawmaker campaigned while touring the whole country.

explain: 한 곳이 아니라 여러 곳을 돌며 방문할 때 쓰고, 한 곳이면 '방문하다'라고 해요. 주로 뉴스에서 정치인이나 고위 인사에게 써요. 목적지는 '을/를'로 받아서 '유럽을 순방하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for visiting several places in turn; for just one place you say '방문하다'. It appears mostly in the news about politicians and high officials. The destination takes 을/를, as in '유럽을 순방하다'.

examples.en: The United States is a longtime ally of our country.
The two countries regard each other as friendly nations.
Representatives of allied countries gathered in Seoul.
They decided to solve the problem in cooperation with allied nations.

examples.ko: 위기가 오면 우방국의 도움이 정말 중요해요.
examples.en: When a crisis comes, help from allies is really important.
The president plans to visit friendly nations one by one.

explain: 뉴스나 외교 이야기에서 나오는 말이에요. 사이가 좋은 나라를 가리키고, 군사 동맹까지 맺은 나라는 '동맹국'이라고 해서 둘이 늘 같지는 않아요. 반대로 사이가 나쁜 나라는 '적대국'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It appears in news and diplomacy talk for countries on good terms. A country with a military alliance is called '동맹국', so the two words are not always the same. Hostile countries are called '적대국'.

en: flow in; be introduced from outside

examples.en: The river water flows into the sea.
Foreign culture came in quickly.
The population moving into the city is growing.

examples.ko: 나쁜 정보가 유입되지 않도록 막아야 해요.
examples.en: We have to block bad information from getting in.

examples.ko: 새로운 자금이 유입되면 회사가 살아날 거예요.
examples.en: If new funds flow in, the company will recover.
The water that got in filled the basement.

explain: 물, 사람, 돈, 문화, 정보처럼 바깥에서 안으로 흘러 들어올 때 써요. 반대말은 '유출되다'예요. 일상에서는 '들어오다'를 쓰고, 뉴스나 통계에서 '유입'과 '유출'을 짝으로 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when water, people, money, culture, or information flows from outside to inside. The opposite is '유출되다'. In daily speech people say '들어오다' instead, while in news and statistics you see '유입' and '유출' as a pair.

examples.en: I saw a joint army, navy and air force exercise on the news.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 육해공군 중에서 공군에 가고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: My uncle wanted to join the air force out of the army, navy and air force.
The commander in chief of the armed forces is the president.
The army, navy and air force all took part in this event.
Army, navy and air force uniforms are on display at the museum.

examples.ko: 육해공군에서 일하는 군인들을 위한 행사가 열렸어요.
examples.en: An event was held for soldiers serving in the army, navy and air force.

explain: 육군, 해군, 공군을 한꺼번에 말할 때 한 단어로 붙여 써요. '삼군'이라고도 말해요. 뉴스나 행사 소식에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It bundles the army, navy and air force into a single word, written without spaces. People also say '삼군'. You often hear it in the news and in reports about events.

examples.en: I took photos with my friends in front of the assembly hall.
There is a very large assembly building in Yeouido.
The lawmakers gathered at the assembly hall and began the meeting.
On our school trip we went to Seoul and toured the assembly building.

examples.ko: 의사당 건물은 밖에서 보면 정말 웅장해요.
examples.en: The assembly building looks really grand from the outside.
I took a walk in a park near the assembly hall.

explain: 우리나라에서는 보통 '국회의사당'이라고 해요. 그냥 '의사당'은 의회가 모여 일하는 건물을 말해요. 병원의 '의사'와는 관계가 없는 말이에요.
explain_en: In Korea people usually say '국회의사당' (National Assembly building). '의사당' alone means the building where a legislature meets. It has nothing to do with '의사' (doctor).

examples.en: That singer is now a nationwide star.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 빵집이 전국구 맛집으로 유명해졌어요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood bakery became famous as a nationally known place.

examples.ko: 예전에는 국회의원 선거에서 전국구 의원을 따로 뽑았어요.
examples.en: In the past, national-seat lawmakers were elected separately in National Assembly elections.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 인맥이 전국구라서 모르는 사람이 없어요.
examples.en: His connections are nationwide, so there's practically no one he doesn't know.
I happened to meet a YouTuber known nationwide.

examples.ko: 동네에서 유명한 가게가 전국구가 되는 건 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy for a famous local shop to become nationally known.

explain: 일상에서는 어떤 사람이나 가게가 전국적으로 유명하다는 구어체 느낌으로 써요. 원래는 선거에서 전국을 한 구역으로 보고 뽑는 의원을 가리켰는데, 요즘 선거 기사에서는 '비례대표'라는 말이 더 일반적이에요.
explain_en: In daily life it is used colloquially to say that a person or shop is famous nationwide. Originally it referred to lawmakers elected with the whole country treated as one district, but in current election news '비례대표' is the more common term.

examples.en: He took part in the war at nineteen.
Before going to war, he left a letter to his family.
Our country was also asked to join the war.
It is a day to honor the soldiers who fought in the war.
It is a story of people who went abroad and fought in the war.
They say he agonized for a long time over whether to join the war.

explain: '전쟁에 참전하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 일반 대회나 행사에는 '참가하다', '참여하다'를 써요. 이미 전쟁이라는 뜻이 들어 있어서 '전쟁에'를 빼도 말이 통해요.
explain_en: Used with the particle '에', as in '전쟁에 참전하다'. For ordinary contests or events, use '참가하다' or '참여하다'. Since the idea of war is already inside the word, it still works even if you drop '전쟁에'.

examples.en: It was a small accident, but its effects spread across the country.
Exchange rate changes spread their effect to small and medium businesses too.

examples.ko: 그 소식이 퍼지면서 불안감이 시장에 파급되었어요.
examples.en: As the news spread, anxiety spread through the market.

examples.ko: 이 정책이 어디까지 파급될지 아직 몰라요.
examples.en: We don't know yet how far this policy's effects will reach.

examples.ko: 유행이 다른 나라로 파급되는 데 오래 걸리지 않았어요.
examples.en: It didn't take long for the trend to spread to other countries.

examples.ko: 문제가 파급되기 전에 빨리 막아야 해요.
examples.en: We have to stop the problem quickly before it spreads.

explain: 영향, 효과, 충격이 다른 곳으로 퍼져 나갈 때 쓰고, 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 많이 나와요. '퍼지다'보다 딱딱하고, 보통 '파급 효과'나 '영향이 파급되다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when an influence, effect or shock spreads to other places, and is common in news and economic talk. It is stiffer than '퍼지다', and usually appears as '파급 효과' or '영향이 파급되다'.

en: give back; return; restore; reduce to

examples.en: The company gives its profits back to society.

examples.ko: 그 부자는 재산을 사회에 환원하기로 했어요.
examples.en: That rich man decided to give his wealth back to society.
I want to give back the help I received to my neighbors.

examples.ko: 복잡한 문제를 하나의 원인으로 환원하면 오해가 생겨요.
examples.en: Reducing a complicated problem to a single cause leads to misunderstanding.
Iron is obtained by reducing iron oxide.
A part of the earnings was given back to the fans.

explain: 환원하다는 얻은 이익이나 도움을 다시 돌려줄 때 '사회에 환원하다'로 가장 많이 써요. '돌려주다'보다 격식이 있고 기부, 나눔의 느낌이 있어요. 과학 시간에는 산소를 떼어 내는 반응을 '환원하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its most common use is '사회에 환원하다', giving back gains or help you received. It is more formal than '돌려주다' (return) and carries a sense of donation and sharing. In science class, it also names the reaction that removes oxygen from a substance.
